first.rationale: Onboarding completion and activation are both declining, and prior evidence indicates that signup simplification and shorter onboarding improve early activation and time-to-value. This offers a direct response to two current problems and a stronger sustainable-revenue path than immediately matching competitor pricing. Verify the pricing record as a comparator because SMB price pressure is material, while testing onboarding with guardrails on qualified pipeline, conversion, retention, and revenue quality.

final.rationale: Run a controlled onboarding simplification experiment focused on self-serve SMB accounts, prioritizing the shortening of the onboarding flow and removing only nonessential signup fields. This directly addresses the 4% completion decline and 6% activation decline, supported by confirmed improvements in completion, time-to-value, and activation. Monitor qualified revenue, 30-day retention, and first meaningful action as guardrails; the signup simplification record showed a small retention decline. Do not use promotional pricing: its 18% qualified-revenue lift was not sustainable because retention fell 12% and the cohort failed at renewal.
